primitives.name: Expected Possession Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: This paper introduces a Bayesian approach for estimating in-game hometeam win probability for Division-I FBS college (American) football that uses expected number of remaining possessions and expected score as two predictors.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\psi_{k,m}': 'Expected number of possessions for team k in season m', 'p_i': 'Probability of possession i', 't_i': 'Time duration of possession i'}
primitives.assumptions: Possession durations are independent and identically distributed; game tempo is stationary within a season.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When possession data is unavailable or corrupted, model defaults to historical averages.

layer2.mapping: Maps observed possession counts to expected future possessions via iterative update rules.
layer2.telemetry: Residual error between actual and expected possessions per game.

primitives.name: Bayesian Win Probability Estimator
primitives.verbatim_quote: [9, 10] establish Bayesian methods for estimating home-team in-game win probability for college and NBA basketball.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P(W|S, T)': 'Posterior probability of home team winning given score S and time T', 'P(S, T|W)': 'Likelihood of observing score and time given win state W', 'P(W)': 'Prior probability of home team winning'}
primitives.assumptions: Conditional independence of score and time given win state; prior follows beta distribution.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When score or time data is missing, posterior collapses to prior belief.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSI's Bayesian inference engine, applying dynamic priors to evolving game states.
layer2.telemetry: Conformal prediction intervals around estimated win probabilities.

primitives.name: Temporal Score Predictor
primitives.verbatim_quote: These, along with other predictors are introduced into two Bayesian approaches for the final estimate of in-game home-team win probability.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\hat{S}(t)': 'Predicted score at time t', '\\alpha': 'Baseline score offset', '\\beta': 'Rate of scoring change per unit time', '\\Delta S(t)': 'Score differential at time t'}
primitives.assumptions: Linear relationship between time and score evolution; score differentials are normally distributed.
primitives.breakdown_regime: During sudden score changes or timeouts, predictor may lag behind actual dynamics.

layer2.mapping: Derives expected score trajectory from current game state for probabilistic forecasting.
layer2.telemetry: Mean squared error between predicted and actual score trajectories.

The model assumes independence among possessions and normality of score differentials, which may break down during high-intensity moments or under unusual game conditions.
